policy_status.new_local_plan_system: in force from 25 March 2026; legacy/new transition during 2026
policy_status.nppf_78c: decision-making buffer provision applies from 1 July 2026 where criteria are met
policy_status.bng_future_change: 0.2ha-or-below exemption change takes effect 6 August 2026; not applied early

batches.t: Current NPPF vs 2025 consultation-draft status gate
batches.c: The operative NPPF remains the 12 December 2024 framework with the 7 February 2025 technical amendment; the December 2025 text is consultation draft and must not be treated as adopted/current decision policy.

The new local-plan regulations took effect from 25 March 2026 while legacy and new systems operate in parallel during 2026. Candidate scoring must use the plan actually applicable to the site and correct statutory stage.
National sustainable-development policy is a decision framework, not a parcel attribute. The applicable development plan, material considerations and proposal facts must be resolved first.
Strategic plan policies and evidence establish area-wide direction. Candidate use requires the correct plan geography, current stage and exact site-policy relationship.
Decision rules operate on a submitted proposal and valid application record. A parcel coordinate alone cannot establish validation, determination route or permission outcome.
Housing supply and delivery are authority-level tests. They may affect decision policy weight but do not make an individual candidate deliverable or permitted.
Local housing need is an unconstrained area-level minimum and is distinct from the plan housing requirement and parcel capacity. No housing-need number is transferred directly to a candidate.
HELAA identifies potential land supply; assessment or inclusion is not allocation or permission. Exact site identity and latest assessment outcome are required.
Economic need and employment land evidence are strategic. Candidate use requires exact employment-site or policy designation and current local-plan implementation.
Sequential and impact tests depend on use, scale, location, available alternatives and locally set thresholds. A parcel is not scored from proximity to a centre alone.
Health and community infrastructure requirements depend on population, proposal impact and local evidence. Area-wide health need is not parcel capacity.

batches.t: Open-space / recreation / Local Green Space gate
batches.c: Open-space policy requires exact protected-space, need and proposal relationship. Borough-level provision or nearby open space is not candidate-specific evidence.
Transport Statements/Assessments and Travel Plans depend on trip generation, network context and proposal scale. Strategic accessibility alone is not a permission result.
National policy supports high-quality communications networks, but site capacity or mast/fibre availability requires exact network and proposal evidence.
Making effective use of land requires reconciling suitability, contamination, stability, existing use and policy. No single strategic evidence source proves developability.
Design policy and national design guidance shape proposal quality. They do not create a parcel capacity result without a scheme, context and applicable local design policy.

batches.t: Green Belt / grey belt / Golden Rules gate
batches.c: Green Belt and grey-belt policy requires exact current boundary, contribution assessment, sustainable-location evidence and where relevant Golden Rules. Borough presence is insufficient.
Climate policy requires location and proposal-specific mitigation/adaptation evidence. Strategic climate policy is not a direct parcel score.
Renewable-energy acceptability depends on technology, scale, location, cumulative effects and proposal details. General policy support is not site permission.
Flood-zone, climate allowance, sequential/exception tests and FRA needs must be resolved against current spatial data and proposal vulnerability; strategic policy alone is insufficient.
Natural-environment policy requires exact designated-site, habitat/species and proposal pathways. Inventory gaps or nearby records are not negative/positive parcel proof.
Heritage policy requires exact asset/setting relationship and proposal effect. National heritage policy or nearby assets cannot be transferred to a candidate.
Mineral safeguarding and extraction policy depends on exact resource/safeguarding geography, mineral authority policy and proposal conflict. National minerals policy is not parcel proof.
Conditions attach to permissions and must satisfy policy/legal tests. A condition cannot be assumed without an exact permission/decision record.
Planning obligations are proposal-specific mitigation and legally bind land interests. Candidate liability requires an exact agreement/application relationship.
CIL liability depends on the charging schedule, chargeable development, floorspace, reliefs/exemptions and timing. Authority CIL presence alone does not establish parcel liability.
Viability evidence is scheme- and policy-context dependent. Plan-level viability or standardised inputs cannot be promoted to a candidate without site-specific scheme facts.
EIA applies only where the regulations and likely significant effects trigger it. Screening depends on development type, scale, location and effects, not parcel identity alone.
BNG is proposal-specific and subject to exemptions/effective-date rules. Current guidance notes a 6 August 2026 small-development change; future rules are not applied early.
Contamination relevance depends on former use, contaminant-pathway-receptor evidence and proposal sensitivity. Strategic or historic land-use context is not proof of contamination.
Land stability requires exact hazard and geotechnical evidence. Suspected mining/subsidence context triggers investigation but is not itself a development refusal.
Air quality and noise are location- and proposal-sensitive material considerations. AQMA/noise context must be tied to baseline, receptors, emissions/noise sources and mitigation.
